data.narrative:
BRINC Drones, a Series C-stage defense and security company founded by Blake Resnick, has raised $157M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a peer set of 10 comparables—2 public (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS) and 8 private firms including Castelion, Stark Defence, and Neros operating in the same sector and stage.

Two valuation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis uses the $157M total raised as a proxy base and applies a 1.7x multiplier typical of Series C advancement, yielding $267M. Peer-median analysis examines three same-stage, same-sector comparables with valuations ranging from $2.5B (Neros) to $13.0B (Castelion), establishing a median of $4.0B. The wide peer range reflects heterogeneity in technology maturity, customer concentration, and addressable market capture within the defense and security space.

Triangulation across these two methods produces a valuation range of $227M (low) to $4.6B (high), with a median of $2.1B. The substantial gap between stage-progression ($267M) and peer-median ($4.0B) reflects the early-stage fundraising proxy relative to comparable companies' demonstrated traction and market positioning. Key uncertainties include BRINC's customer concentration and contract durability in a sector sensitive to procurement cycles, as well as the applicability of high-valuation outliers (Castelion at $13B) given potential differences in deployment scale and strategic positioning.
